name: Dewas-Done Danuwar
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only classification/survey refs (Hodgson 1857, van Driem 2001, Shackelford et al. 2018 sociolinguistic survey); no grammar/phonology of Dewas-Done Danuwar found

sources.citation: Kuegler, Klaus P. & Doris Kuegler. 1974. Danuwar Rai Phonemic Summary. Kathmandu: Summer Institute of Linguistics & Institute of Nepal and Asian Studies, Tribhuvan University. ix+91 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 36926)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: HathiTrust digitized, search-only (in copyright); interlibrary loan (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: No stress/accent section (TOC: Introduction, Consonants, Vowels, Syllables, Appendix). p.75: 'In Danuwar Rai there is no contrast between long and short vowels.. Special emphasis is signified by rising pitch, heavy stress, and extra length of vowel. (See Bandhu 1971:46-47.)'; p.77 passing remark that a di-syllabic word has 'different stress and rhythm characteristics than a tri-syllabic word like /talau/'. Nothing on which syllable bears word stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PK115.I23 2011); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PK115 .I23 2011
sources.note: 5.1.0 p.292: vowel length non-distinctive, used for emphasis (taro [taro] 'far' ~ [taːro] 'very far'); then explicitly 'Супрасегментные характеристики в Д.я. не исследованы.' (Suprasegmental characteristics of Danuwar have not been investigated.) No stress statement.

sources.citation: Shackelford, Sarah. 2019. A Sociolinguistic Study of Dewas Rai and Danuwar. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2019-009. Dallas: SIL International. 162 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (sociolinguistic survey + wordlists). Used for identity: p.4 Kuegler & Kuegler 1974 worked 'in an area now known to be Dewas Rai'; Kavre/Panchkhal = Done/Danuwar variety.

sources.citation: Regmi, Ambika & Indresh Thakur. 2016. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Danuwar. Report submitted to the Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.9 literature review (after Eppele et al. 2012/Ethnologue): 'It is a non-tonal language. There are 29 consonant and 6 vowel phonemes in the language.' p.8 notes Timilsina & Das 2008 includes a sketch grammar covering phonology.
